diagnostic_evidence.quote:
governed by the 
inverse Hessian~$H^{-1}$ of the inner objective.

issues.failure_explanation: The formula defines H as the gradient ∇_θ R̂_m (a vector) while calling H⁻¹ the 'inverse Hessian' (a matrix), and the last factor is ∇²_θ R̂_j (an n×n Hessian) where the correct hypergradient requires ∇_θ R̂_j (an n-vector). As written, the product (∇_θ C)ᵀ H⁻¹ ∇²_θ R̂_j yields a vector, not the scalar ∂C/∂γ_j that the left-hand side requires.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace ∇²_θ R̂_j(θ⋆) with ∇_θ R̂_j(θ⋆) and redefine H as ∇²_θ R̂_m(θ⋆,γ) (the Hessian of the inner objective).
issues.overall_effect: The stated hypergradient formula for bilevel loss-weight balancing is dimensionally inconsistent and does not compute the claimed quantity. Any implementation or further derivation relying on this expression is unreliable.
issues.title: Hypergradient formula confuses gradient and Hessian in two places
issues.why_classification: The fix is a local swap of two symbols (gradient ↔ Hessian) in a single displayed formula; the surrounding bilevel formulation and its interpretation remain intact.

issues.failure_explanation: The summand inside the inner sum over j uses the index i in both the norm ‖γ_i ∇R̂_i‖ and the rate r_i^ζ, so the summand is independent of j. The inner sum therefore collapses to N times the summand divided by N, i.e. ‖γ_i ∇R̂_i‖·r_i^ζ, reducing the whole objective to ∑_i ‖γ_i ∇R̂_i‖·|1−r_i^ζ|, which is not the GradNorm equalisation surrogate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the inner sum to average over j: replace the summand with ‖γ_j ∇_θ R̂_j(θ)‖ (and move r_i^ζ outside or keep it as the per-component weight).
issues.overall_effect: The described GradNorm loss-balancing procedure does not minimise the intended surrogate; the formula as written cannot equalise per-loss gradient magnitudes as claimed in the surrounding prose.
issues.title: GradNorm surrogate objective has degenerate inner sum (wrong index)
issues.why_classification: The correction is a local index fix in one displayed formula; the algorithmic concept (equalising weighted gradient norms) and all surrounding prose remain valid.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: is said to be smooth if there exists $L>0$ such that, for all $\theta_1,\theta_2\in \mathbb{R}^n$

issues.failure_explanation: The definition introduces a constant L > 0 but the Lipschitz condition on the gradient omits it, reading ‖∇f(θ₁)−∇f(θ₂)‖ ≤ ‖θ₁−θ₂‖, which is 1-smoothness rather than L-smoothness. Consequently the phrase 'L_i-smooth' used in Assumption hp_smooth has no meaning relative to this definition, and every theorem that bounds the step size by L_max is stated under an incoherent hypothesis.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the factor L on the right-hand side of the inequality: ‖∇f(θ₁)−∇f(θ₂)‖ ≤ L‖θ₁−θ₂‖.
issues.overall_effect: The smoothness assumption and all four SGD convergence theorems that invoke L_max in their step-size conditions are technically stated under a definition that does not parameterise the smoothness constant, making the hypotheses incoherent as written.
issues.title: Definition of smoothness omits the Lipschitz constant L
issues.why_classification: A single-symbol insertion repairs the definition; all theorem statements, step-size conditions, and proof arguments remain correct once the definition matches standard L-smoothness.

issues.failure_explanation: The loss components f_i are indexed by i = 1, …, m (the m data samples in problem (2)), but L_max is defined as max_{i=1,…,n} L_i, where n is the parameter dimension. If m ≠ n the expression references L_{m+1}, …, L_n (undefined) or omits L_{n+1}, …, L_m, making L_max either ill-defined or incorrect.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the upper index from n to m: L_max := max_{i=1,…,m} L_i.
issues.overall_effect: Every convergence theorem that imposes a step-size bound in terms of L_max (α < 1/(2L_max), α ≤ 1/(4L_max), α₀ ≤ 1/(4L_max), etc.) is stated under a misdefined constant, so the hypotheses are not the intended ones.
issues.title: L_max defined as max over n indices instead of m
issues.why_classification: A single-index correction in the assumption; all downstream step-size conditions and convergence rates are unchanged once L_max refers to the correct set of m smoothness constants.

issues.failure_explanation: The intermediate line claims E_k‖θ_{k+1}−θ⋆‖² ≤ (1−αμ) − 2α(f(θ_k)−f(θ⋆)) + α_k²σ². The right-hand side is dimensionally inconsistent: (1−αμ) is a bare scalar missing the factor ‖θ_k−θ⋆‖², and the function-difference term does not arise from the strong-convexity bound at this stage. The correct intermediate step should read (1−αμ)‖θ_k−θ⋆‖² + α²E_k‖∇f_{i_k}‖² − 2α⟨∇f, θ_k−θ⋆⟩, from which the subsequently stated 'main recursion' follows.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the garbled line with the correct strong-convexity + smoothness bound: E_k‖θ_{k+1}−θ⋆‖² ≤ (1−αμ)‖θ_k−θ⋆‖² + α²‖∇f(θ_k)‖² + α²σ², then proceed to the main recursion.
issues.overall_effect: The logical chain in the proof of thm:added-1 is broken at this line; as written the inequality does not follow from the preceding expansion nor lead to the 'main recursion' stated immediately after.
issues.title: Garbled intermediate inequality in proof of strongly-convex SGD theorem
issues.why_classification: The theorem statement and the 'main recursion' used in the geometric-series summation are both correct; only one intermediate display needs to be rewritten. No change to the conclusion or to any dependent result is required.

issues.failure_explanation: θ̄_K is the (weighted) average of all iterates up to time K and does not depend on the index k. Hence min_{k=0,…,K−1} E‖∇f(θ̄_K)‖² = E‖∇f(θ̄_K)‖², making the minimisation vacuous. The standard nonconvex SGD guarantee bounds min_{k=0,…,K−1} E‖∇f(θ_k)‖² (individual iterates), not the gradient at the final averaged point. As stated, the theorem either asserts a trivial repetition or, if read as an ergodic nonconvex bound E‖∇f(θ̄_K)‖² ≤ C/√K, a claim that does not hold without additional structure (e.g. convexity).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace θ̄_K with θ_k inside the minimum to state the standard nonconvex SGD result min_{k=0,…,K−1} E‖∇f(θ_k)‖² ≤ C/√K, or remove the min and provide the additional hypotheses needed for an ergodic bound.
issues.overall_effect: The nonconvex convergence guarantee is not the standard O(1/√K) stationarity result; the stated bound is either vacuous or unsupported for nonconvex objectives.
issues.title: Nonconvex SGD bound uses vacuous min over k of gradient at averaged iterate
issues.why_classification: Changing θ̄_K to θ_k (a one-symbol edit) recovers the well-known nonconvex SGD guarantee with the same O(1/√K) rate; no new proof architecture is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Each function $f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ in problem \eqref{eq:min_problem} is $L_i$-smooth. Denote $L_{\max}:=\max_{i=1,\dots,n} L_i$.

issues.failure_explanation: The constant L_f appears in both the step-size prescription and the right-hand-side bound, but it is never defined anywhere in the paper. The only smoothness constants introduced are L_i (per-component) and L_max. Without a definition, the theorem's hypothesis (the step-size condition) and its conclusion (the bound) are incomplete: the reader cannot verify that the step size is admissible or evaluate the rate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define L_f as the global smoothness constant of f (e.g. L_f = (1/m)∑_i L_i ≤ L_max) in the theorem's hypothesis or in Assumption hp_smooth, and verify that the resulting step size α = √(2/(L_f L_max K)) satisfies the standard nonconvex SGD requirement.
issues.overall_effect: The nonconvex SGD convergence theorem is stated with an undefined parameter; its step-size condition and iteration-complexity bound cannot be checked or used as written.
issues.title: Undefined constant L_f in nonconvex SGD theorem step size and bound
issues.why_classification: The repair requires introducing a new defined quantity and confirming that the step-size and bound remain consistent with the standard nonconvex SGD analysis; it is more than a single-symbol typo but does not require new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The bound in the nonconvex theorem contains the term Δ_f^⋆, but the only quantity defined in the theorem is Δ_f := inf f − (1/m)∑ inf f_i. No relationship between Δ_f^⋆ and Δ_f is stated, and Δ_f^⋆ does not appear elsewhere in the paper. The expression is therefore undefined as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Δ_f^⋆ with Δ_f (the quantity defined in the same theorem), or add a definition of Δ_f^⋆ if it is intended to differ.
issues.overall_effect: The right-hand side of the nonconvex SGD bound is incomplete; the value of the stationarity guarantee cannot be evaluated without knowing what Δ_f^⋆ is.
issues.title: Nonconvex SGD bound references undefined Δ_f^⋆ instead of defined Δ_f
issues.why_classification: The most natural reading is that Δ_f^⋆ is a notational slip for Δ_f; correcting the symbol restores a complete, evaluable bound with no change to the rate or the proof structure.
